parts.text: I'm planning a small task-tracker app for a team of five. Help me pick a stack.
A TypeScript API on Node with a React front end keeps one language across the app. The open question is storage.
Let's use SQLite for storage. It is one file and we have no one to run a database server.
SQLite fits that well. A minimal schema:
Change of plan: three offices will write at the same time and the client wants managed backups. Is SQLite still right?
No. Switch to Postgres for storage: SQLite allows one writer at a time, and a managed Postgres gives you backups. The schema ports with small changes (SERIAL id, BOOLEAN done).
OK. My draft .env has DATABASE_URL=postgres://app@localhost:5432/tasks and API_KEY=sk-proj-FAKEFAKEFAKEFAKEFAKE1234. Send the hosting invoice to jane.doe@example.com.
Do not commit that key; load it from the environment at runtime. Next steps: provision Postgres, migrate the schema, then schedule backups.
